script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Workplace
Theme: small-town life

Begin screenplay.

FADE IN:

INT. MILLTOWN BAKERY - MORNING

JESSICA (mid 30s, warm, friendly) is arranging pastries on the counter as RACHEL (early 30s, efficient, meticulous) cleans the espresso machine. The doors swing open, revealing ROBERT (late 40s, kind-hearted, quiet) with a delivery box.

JESSICA
Good morning, Robert! The fresh bread arrived just in time.

ROBERT
Morning, Jessica. Rachel, how's the machine behaving?

RACHEL
(looking up)
Good as new, thank you, Robert.

Jessica hands Robert a few dollars. Robert nods and exits.

JESSICA
Alrighty, we're open!

INT. MILLTOWN BAKERY - DAY

The shop is bustling. Customers line up for coffee and pastries. Amidst the chaos, CAROLINE (early 20s, ambitious, perfectionist) joins Jessica and Rachel.

CAROLINE
Good morning, ladies. I'll be taking over the register today.

RACHEL
Morning, Caroline. Be sure to take breaks. You can't make change if you're not here.

JESSICA
Absolutely, Caroline. And remember, a smile goes a long way.

INT. MILLTOWN BAKERY - LUNCH RUSH

The bakery is packed with customers. The team works together efficiently, serving coffee and pastries, restocking shelves, and taking orders. The clock strikes 1 pm, and the lunch rush begins to subside.

RACHEL
(to Jessica and Caroline)
Great work, ladies. We made it through the lunch rush.

JESSICA
Agreed. Let's take a few minutes to clean up before the afternoon rush.

INT. MILLTOWN BAKERY - AFTERNOON

Jessica, Rachel, and Caroline clean and restock. They exchange pleasantries with customers and make small talk. A knock on the door signals another delivery.

JESSICA
(to Caroline)
You got this. I'll take care of the new delivery.

Caroline nods as Jessica steps out.

INT. MILLTOWN BAKERY - DELIVERY AREA

Jessica opens the door to reveal MIKE (early 40s, jovial, friendly) with a delivery of fresh produce. They chat about their families and small-town life as they unload the delivery.

MIKE
(pulling out a bouquet of flowers)
I have a little something for you, Jessica.

JESSICA
(smiling)
How thoughtful! These will look beautiful on the counter.

INT. MILLTOWN BAKERY - END OF DAY

As the sun begins to set, the shop starts to empty out. The team cleans up and counts the day's earnings.

CAROLINE
(to Jessica and Rachel)
Another successful day.

JESSICA
Indeed, Caroline. Thanks to your hard work.

RACHEL
We couldn't have done it without the whole team.

The three share a smile, knowing that they've come together to create a warm, welcoming space in their small town.

FADE OUT.
